1. with, Bausyi bakali kunyema kufwumbwa babona mwanaabo musimbi kaenda amusankwa. = Her father was angry whenever he saw his daughter walking with a boy. Aano mazuba tupona muciindi ncotulibonena ameso eesu mbuli zintu mbozisanduka. = Nowadays we live in a time when we see with our own eyes how things change.
  2. on, Civwubwe tajisi boya amubili. = The hippo does not have hair on it's body. Kobikka zisani zyangu abulo. = Put my clothes on the bed.
  3. and, Moonga a Cheepa bakaunka ku Monze. = Moonga and Cheepa went to Monze.
  4. of, Bacibize mmabbiza amusyokwe. = Zebras are the horses of the bush. (Note: if three vowels occur, one is elided) Isumo lyamwami ndilamfwu. = The spear of the chief is long.
  5. at, Nibakasika amunzi bakalikatede. = When they arrived at the village, they were tired.

1. for, Aaya mmasembe aacibwa- ntu. = These roughly crushed grains are for sweet-beer.
  2. of, Masizi aamulilo alapya. = The embers of the fire are hot. Mayi aankuku mmabotu kulya. = The eggs of chickens are good to eat.
1. these (mu-ba noun-class) Aaba bana balakatazya. = These children are troublesome.
1. those, Aabo bayanda kulwana. = Those want to fight.
1. (exclamation) conveys surprise, disappointment, disapproval etc. depending on context.
1. near, Mwiinga wakalikukkala afwiifwi amunzi wa Haakoola. = Mwiinga was living near the village of Haakoola
1. this one, Aaka kana kalasesya. = This child is amusing.

1. later on, Basicikolo balalya akale, kutali ino. = The pupils will eat later on, not now. Tulabonana akale, zuba licili lipati. = We will see one another later on, the sun is still high. Tulaunka akale kumuunda, ileke mvwula. = We will go later to the field, let the rain stop.
1. that one, Kokaleta kana ako. = Bring that little child here.
1. his/hers, Mapopwe aakwe akaligwa nombe. = His maize was eaten by the cattle.

1. they also, Zitende zyakaunka mulonga, aalo matanga akaunka. = The pumpkins were taken away by the river, the melons were taken as well.
  2. only, Insima yamana mucibiya, kwacaala makololo aalo. = The nsima is finished in the pot, there remains only the leavings.

1. that time, Cakali ciindi camangolezya, aalya bantu mpobamanina kulya nsima. = It was evening time, that very time when people finish eating nsima.
  2. those over there. Aalya makwaambala alalula. = Those cucumbers over there are bitter.
1. these over here, Aaya makwaambala alalula. = These cucumbers here are bitter. Maaya aya balaayanda bamacembele. = These stringedskirts here are wanted by the old women.

1. those, Bantu banji bakali kuyoowa masiku aayo. = Many people were afraid during those nights.
  2. those, that, Kamubapa mango aayo bana balye. = Give those mangoes to the children so that they eat.
1. these, Banyama aba mbakali. = These animals are fierce.
1. they also, with them, Bakatalika abalaabo kwiimba ciimbo. = They also began to sing a song. Also: abalo
1. they also, with them, Boombe baunka abalo musyokwe. = The calves have also gone into the bush. Also: abalabo
1. these here, Abano bantu bayanda kunduuma. = These people here want to beat me.

1. those, those yonder, Basimbi abaya bazyana kabotu. = Those girls over there are dancing well. abo their, Boonse bakapiluka kumaanda abo. = All returned to their homes.
  2. those, Kobaleta bana abo baone. = Bring those children so that they sleep.
1. as a result of, consequently, Ijilo yakawa mvwula, aboobo bantu batalika kulima sunu. = Yesterday the rain fell, and so today the people have begun to plough.
1. it also, they also, Bulimi abulabo mmulimo. = Farming is also hard work. Also: abwalo
1. it also, they also, Bukoko obu bwakapapa abwalo. = This beer is also stale.
1. it also, Cisuwo eeci ncibotu acalo. = This basket is also beautiful.
1. (exclamation) Accu kaka! walijaya iji! = Oh dear! You have broken the egg.
1. it also, Kamucileta acilaco cisuwo eeco. = Bring along also that basket. Also: acalo
1. it also, with it, Kounka aco cibango ukabelesye. = Go also with the shallow basket so that you can use it.
1. Also: afwiifwi
1. near, Ndikkala afwiifwi aku Chikuni. = I live near to Chikuni. Also: afwaafwi.
1. the time when all sleep, Sunu mwezi ulamuka kuzwa. Cifwumo uyakuzwa agonamukunu. Today the moon is slow to come out. Tomorrow it will appear when all are sleep.
1. the time when childen sleep, Mwezi ono wakaindide kale agonancece. (aalya aonena bana). = The moon by then had already gone past the time when childen sleep.
1. the time when adults sleep, Wakali kuyanda kusika agonankalamba, (aalya aonena bapati.) = He wanted to arrive at the time when the elders sleep.
1. (exclamation)
1. it also, Ailayo nombe eyi ilijisi mukupa. = This cow also has milk. Also: ayalo.
1. this little, Kasankwa aka kalijisi maanu. = This little boy has intelligence.
1. because of, Akaambo kamvwula yakawa jilo, sunu bantu batalika kulima. = Because of the rain which fell yesterday, today the people have begun to plough.

1. because of the fact that, Akaambo kakuti yakabusya muyoba, kunyina naba omwe wakazwa kuya kumyuunda buzuba oobo. = Because of the fact that a cloud-cover had arisen, not even one person went out to go to the fields that day.
1. this little, (ka-tu noun-class), Kana aka kalaciswa. = This little child is sick.
1. (exclamation of pleading) Ndakomba akaka baama mutanduumi! = Please mother do not beat me!
1. and she/he also, Akalako kasimbi aaka kalijisi maanu. = And that little girl also has intelligence. Also: akalo, akalo aka
1. obviously, Akale inga waangwa kuti kobba. = Obviously you will be arrested if you steal.
1. it, he/she (little) also, Kalobo kangu kakatolwa nswi akalo. = My hook was also taken by the fish. Akalo kana kangu kakalemba musunko. = My child also wrote the exam.
1. a little, Nsemuyandi akaniini pe. = I do not like him even a little bit.
1. this here, Akano kazyiba kajisi nswi zinji. = This pool here has many fish. Kooye akano nkayumu kapati. = This cord here is very strong.
1. in the middle, Mwana unyonka uwona akati. = A suckling-child sleeps between. (the father and mother)
1. in the middle of, between, Musankwa ooyu ulayanda kukkala akati kabasimbi. = This boy likes to sit among the girls. Chisekesi cili akati ka Monze a Pemba. = Chisekesi is between Monze and Pemba.
1. that, that yonder, Akaya kalundu nkalamfwu. = That yonder hill is high. Kabwa akaya kaciswa cinsuungwe. = That dog over there has rabies.
1. that, Kokatapula kauka ako, kalaluma mwana. = Shake off that insect, it will bite the baby.
1. it also, (concerning place or activity) Ku Choma nkule akulako. = It is also far to Choma. Kuuma bana nkubi akulako. = Beating children is also bad. Also: akwalo.
1. it also, Ku Choma nkubotu, akwalo ku Monze nkubotu. = It is good at Choma, and it is also good at Monze. Also: akulako
1. and he/she also, Mutinta waunka alakwe kucisobano. = Mutinta also has gone to the concert. Also: awalo.
1. those also, Masuku alanona alao. = Masuku fruits are also sweet. Also: aalo.
1. where? Mutinta, wacibikka ali cisuwo? Mutinta, where did you put the basket?
1. he/she only, alone, Mwaaba ngusimweenda alikke. = The jackal is one who travels alone.
1. it also, Alilayo ji eeli lyafwa. = This egg also is broken. cf. alyalo.
1. again, further, moreover, Wakatalika alimwi kuyeeya. = He started to think again.

1. only, merely, just, Naakalanga keembe wakamvwa mwida moonse aba meenda alo. = When he looked at the axe he felt everywhere in his stomach becoming just water. Mubutala kuli maila muceme alo. = In the maize-bin there is only sorgum.
1. it also, Alulao lubalo olu ndubotu. = This wattle is also good. Allso alwalo.
1. it also, Lulabo Iwamvwula lulayoosya alwalo. = Lightning is also frightening.
1. yonder, Kamuya mukalete mabwe alya. = Go and bring those stones yonder. Kotola ukaciyanike citaka alya abala zuba. = Take the small fish and put it out to dry yonder where the sun is shining.
1. it also, Alyalo bbiza eeli ndilya Katowa. = This horse also belongs to Katowa. Liso lyangu lilacisa alyalo. = My eye is also paining.
1. it also, with it, Magwaza waunka alyo bbiza kumuunda. = Magwaza went with the horse also to the field.
1. a place unknown and forgotten, Ndaunka nkafwe amanaamani. = I go so that I die in a place unknown and forgotten.
1. beside, Mutinta wakali kweenda ambali amulonga. = Mutinta was walking beside the river.

<ol><li>I also, <p-eg><p-l>Ambebo ndayanda kulya.</p-l> = I also want to eat.</p-eg>
<ol><li>Also ambebo.

<ol><li>now at present while something goes on, <p-eg><p-l>Ambuliino notwaambaula, sintolongo ulya nsima yasautu.</p-l> = And just now as we talk, the prisoner is eating <p-l>nsima</p-l> with salt as relish.</p-eg>
<ol><li>perhaps, <p-eg><p-l>Amundisilike ambeyo, ambweni ndilapona.</p-l> = Treat me also, perhaps I will be healed.</p-eg> Also <p-l>ndiza</p-l>
<ol><li>I also, <p-eg><p-l>Ame ndalimumvwide walikukanana.</p-l> = I also heard him when he was talking. </p-eg> Also amebo
<ol><li>I also, with me, <p-eg><p-l>Ndakajisi mali manji amebo.</p-l> = I also had much money.</p-eg>

<ol><li>at all, <p-eg><p-l>Sicinsuungwe nsemuyandi amwayinda pe.</p-l> = I do not like a rabid dog at all.</p-eg>
<ol><li>in, also, <p-eg><p-l>Amwalo mubwina oomu mwanjila sulwe.</p-l> = Also in this hole a rabbit has entered.</p-eg>

• together with, Bakali kulida amwi. = They were eating together.
    • some, (ma noun-class) Mapopwe amwi ali kabotu. = Some of the maize is good.
<ol><li>as if, like, <p-eg><p-l>Mwaaba uboneka anga mmubwa.</p-l> = The jackal looks as if it is a dog.
<ol><li>they also, <p-eg><p-l>Mukaboole angawo mabbuku kucikolo.</p-l> = Come to school with the books also.</p-eg> Also <p-l>aalo</p-l>.
<ol><li>my, <p-eg><p-l>Matendaangu mmapati.</p-l> = My feet are big.</p-eg>

(i.e. they are secret- ely carrying out their work of destruction.)</p-eg><p-eg>Ulibonya luuswe-uswe <p-l>ani kuti</p-l> mmubbi wababbi. = He seems to be kind but instead of that he is the thief of thieves.</p-eg>

<ol><li>these here, this here, here, on here, right here, <p-eg>Amulange mango <p-l>ano</p-l>. = Look at these mangoes here.</p-eg><p-eg>Kamuleta nsima <p-l>ano</p-l> tulide mpawo. = Bring the nsima here we will eat it on the spot.</p-eg>

<ol><li>outside, <p-eg>Mubbi wakazwida <p-l>ansengwe</p-l> akutija. = The thief ran outside and fled. Atubandikile <p-l>ansengwe</p-l>.  = Let us talk outside.</p-eg><p-eg>Bulaca mpaansengwe kuzyula milonga. = Going to the toilet many times at night.</p-eg>

<ol><li>on or towards the ground, <p-eg>Munyumbwe utola mukosi <p-l>ansi</p-l> nalunduka. = The gnu lowers its neck towards the ground when it is running.</p-eg><p-eg>Kotula cileye cankuni <p-l>ansi</p-l>. = Put the bundle of firewood down on the ground.</p-eg>

<ol><li>first, <p-eg>Kotaningamujata, <p-l>ansyini</p-l> ndiboole. = Do not catch him, let me come first.</p-eg>
<ol><li>openly, publicly, <p-eg>Milimo mibotu ilacitwa <p-l>antangalala</p-l>. = Good deeds are done in the open.</p-eg>
<ol><li>perhaps, maybe, <p-eg>Kamukumba cibwantu <p-l>antela</p-l> beenzu bayakusika juunza. = Brew sweet-beer, perhaps visitors will come tomorrow.</p-eg>Also anteni, ambweni, ndiza
<ol><li>perhaps, maybe, <p-eg><p-l>Anteni</p-l> ndiyakuunka ku Monze juunza. = Perhaps I will go to Monze tomorrow.</p-eg>Also <p-l>antela</p-l>

<ol><li>together, <p-eg>Mainza, ndakwiita <p-l>antoomwe</p-l> abanyoko kuti tubandike. = Mainza, I have called you  together with your mother to talk. </p-eg><p-eg>Moonze Mukkulu uzikkidwe <p-l>antoomwe</p-l> a Moonze Nchete. Moonze Mukkulu is buried together with Moonze Nchete.<p-eg>
1. (refers to place) Aawa antu alalibonya kuti mapopwe taakomeni. = Here in this place it can be seen that the maize does not grow well.
1. whereas, but, Ndali kuti ooyu ngumangoye anu ninsezi. = I thought that this was a cat, whereas it is a cane rat. Also: ani kuti
1. you also, with you, Bantu banji baya ku Monze mu Nsondo, anywe mukaunke. = Many people are going to Monze on Sunday and you also should go. Also: anywebo.
1. you also, with you, Amukalime anywebo. = You also should plough. Also: anywe.
1. outside, Sena unyina mulimo ngobeleka anze? = Is there no work which you are doing outside?
1. at first, Atulye anzini, tulaunka akale. = Let us eat first, we will go later on.
1. in the middle of the night, Wakasika kunanda anamba yamasiku kakatede kapati. = He arrived home in the middle of the night very tired. Also: ampingano
1. them also, Mangamwe tandaayandi ao. = I do not like cooked whole grains also. Also: aalo
1. we also, Aswe twakazwidilila mumizundano. = We also succeeded in the competitions. Also: aswebo.
1. we also, Basazima nibakali kulila nkobazwa, aswebo twakali kulila umwi muntu. = When our relatives were mourning at their village, we also were mourning for somebody else.
1. on top of, Basilumamba bakayaka mavwuka atalaa mulundu. = The soldiers erected their camp on top of the hill.
1. perhaps, Tatuzyi, atene musololi wabo ulasika. = We do not know, perhaps their leader is arriving. Also: anteni
1. when on the other hand, Mutinta atacikonzyi kweembela ŋombe,
1. Mweemba ucili mwana ulakonzya. = How can Mutinta be unable to herd cattle when on the other hand Mweemba can, who is still young! Also: nokuba kuti
1. their's, Basankwa bapati bakalya mapopwe ato tusimbi tuniini. = The big boys ate the maize of those small girls.
1. they also, Twana twankuku twakafwa atulato. = The chicks also died. Also: atwalo.

1. visible, clear, white, Bantu bakalibabwene babbi nkaambo mulilo wakali kuyaka akubasiya atuba. = The people were viewing the thieves because the fire was shining and left them visible. Inkuku yangu itula mayi atuba bu. = My hen lays very white eggs. Also: antangalala
1. they also, Tuuka atwalo tulamvwana mukubeleka. = Insects also cooperate in working. Tusankwa nitwakalila, atwalo tusimbi twakalila. = When the young boys wept, the young girls also wept.
1. she/he/it also Musune wabataata ulakwela kapati, aulao wabauso mbubona. = The ox of my father pulls very well, and also the one of your father. Also: awalo
1. each one, Sunu aumwi ulandipa busala. = Today each one of you will give me busala tubers.
1. here, on here, Kamubikka zitina awa. = Put the bricks here.
1. he/she also, Bbule awalo ubalilwa kubacele. = The honey-badger is also counted among the soft-footed quadruped animals. Kamumupa cakulya mucete awalo. = Give the poor person also food.
1. over there, Bayanda kuzyana cinande, kabaya awo. = Those who want to dance the cinande, should go over there.
1. it also, they also, Ayalo nombe eyi ilijisi mukupa. = And this cow. also has much milk.
1. you also, Kopandulula ayebo tumvwe. = You also explain so that we listen.
1. that, those, Mabele ayo ngabeenzu. = That finger-millet is for the visitors.
1. these also, Azyalo mpongo eezi zilazyala. = These goats also are prolific.
1. (prefix of respect,) Nobatumbu, kamunyonsya mwana. = You O suckling mother, breast feed the child.
1. these, Tuyanda baaba kuti bakaimbe. = We want these so that they sing.
1. those, Tabali babaya bauma mwana pele mbababaya. = It is not those who have beaten the child but those other ones.
1. his, hers, rt. -akwe, Babwa bakwe bakaluma mpongo yangu jilo. = His/her dogs bit my goat yesterday.
1. they themselves, them, Bausyi baambide bana kuya kumuunda, pele balo tiibaunka. = Their father told the children to go to the field, however they themselves did not go.
1. other ones (ba noun-class), Kakuboola bambi basankwa, mulimo wakomena. = Let other boys come, the work is great.
1. some, Banji basankwa baunka ku Monze, bamwi balalima mu- O - 1296 muunda. = Many boys have gone to Monze, some are ploughing in the field.
1. my, banyama bangu = my animals, (rt. -ngu)
1. not so many people / animals, rt. -njaanji, Ijilo bantu bakali banjaanji bakasika kucikombelo. = Yesterday not so many people came to church.
1. many people/animals (rt. -nji), Banji bantu bafwa nzala mazuba ano. = Many people are suffering from hunger these days.
1. these, these here, Basicikolo bano bamana kale kulemba. = These pupils here have already finished writing. Also: beno.
1. those, Tuuli mukwasyi wakusobanina, ba Muchelemba baya pe! = It is certainly not a family to play with, those Muchelemba's! Baya basankwa tabalilemeki. = Those boys do not respect themselves.
1. describes movement, Mubili mbuwakatontweda buyo, wakabona mabambo nkwaati bbaku-bbaku kuya mujulu ansi cabuteteete. = As the body began to quieten down he saw the ribs moving up and down gently.
1. closely together, Bakakkala bbambwa munsi lyakwe kumwi kaba-mulanga kumeso. = She sat closely together beside him while looking into his eyes.
1. unlucky, Kwajanika kuti mu Monze kwanyina. Aboobo twaakusika aku Chisekese akwalo twaakulyuuma bbi. = We found nothing at Monze and so when we arrived at Chisekesi we were unlucky even there.

1. something very bad or ugly, Basicintoolo bakanduuzya ijansi ibbi ncobeni. = The shop-keeper sold me a very bad coat. bbuntuku fall with a crash, Wakaile kuwa ansi bbuntuku! = He fell to the ground with a bang. Also: -bbu! bbutuku! suddenly, Niyakapya nanda twakabuka bbutuku! Twazwida anze. = When the house caught fire we arose suddenly in haste. We went outside. beni themselves, Bana bamazubaano balalijaya beni, nkaambo tabayandi kulaigwa. = The children of today destroy themselves, because they do not want to be instructed. beno these, these here, Kamubaleka beno bana, baone kuno. = Leave these children here, so that they sleep here.
1. bad, ugly, Kunyina muntu mmubi cakumaninina, amwi buyo ulalombozegwa. = No person is totally bad, from some aspect s/he is worthy of praise.
1. very bad, Muntu mubiibi upenzya bantunyina. = A very bad person persecutes his fellow human beings.
1. second, Kamuleta musune wabili tumaninzye kuvwoleka. = Bring the second ox so that we complete the yoking.

1. unripe, raw, uncooked, Nabwiinga wajika nsima mbisi ucili mweenzu. = The bride has badly cooked the nsima when she is still new in the home. biya (emphatic) indeed, Ndaunka biya kubbola nomuyanda nomutayandi. = I am indeed going to the match whether you like it or not. biyo just, only, simply, Ndajana biyo tutaka mumoono, kunyina mondo. = I just found small fish in the fishing basket, no barbel. bobu this, Moono upatikwa bobu. = This is the way we put the circular stick to finish making the fishing-basket. Also: boobu. bobuya that way, Waakusika munkuta ukaambe bobuya. When you reach the court speak in that way. bolyoo (used with the verb -njila), implies forced and penetrating entry, Inombe yakali kutandwa babwa, yakaile kunjila bolyoo muciba cabantu. = The cow which was being chased by the dogs just entered in a rush into the kraal of other people.

1. very soft, Masuku mabombe aitwa kuti nimbole. = Very soft masuku fruit are called mbole. bongaye? rt. -ngaye, how many? Bongaye basimbi basika? How many girls have arrived? boobo thus, like that, Tacigambyi mboowamba boobo. = It is not surprising that you speak thus. Nooli kwaamba boobo kumatalikilo, nooliluzi. = If you had talked like that at the beginning, you would have been right. boobu thus, like this, Tiindaazyi kuti ciya kuba boobu pe. = I did not expect that it would become like this. Kuti wacita boobu, inanda ilalulama. = If you do like this, the house will be alright.

1. good, beautiful, Muntu mubotu tabuli kampenda. An upright person is not without a fault. Mainza wakali musimbi mubotu. = Mainza was a beautiful girl. bu(u) exceedingly white (with the vb. tuba), Iccuka lituba buu balaliyanda bamwi bantu. = Some people like pure white sugar.

1. while, Wakali kuyabulya musozya naakali kuya kucikolo. = He was eating samp while going to school. bucami deliberately, Catakacitwa bucami. = It was not done deliberately. Also: caali bucedo dawn, Nkuku zilalila kubucedo. Chickens cry at dawn.
1. do something while bending down, Tacipi bulemu kulya bukofwu. = It is not dignified to eat while bending down.

1. unenergetic, Mainza mpaabonenwa babukoole, baabo batakonzyi kutambisya basune, balo banga koonse kujata jamba lyagombe nkwiide kudadalika. = In the rainy season is where the unenergetic ones are seen, those who cannot control oxen, and those who when they hold a plough just stagger about.

1. open, Utasiyi bukwazi munanda. = Do not leave the door ajar. Yakaboola mvwula kajisi guwo pati lyalo ilyakapa kuyoowa kupati kubantu kuti maanda abo alacaala bukwazi kaatajisi ziluli. = The rain came with a mighty wind making the people fear greatly that their houses would be left open without roofs.
1. at this time, Bulwazi buliino bulanyenaanzya kapati. = The contemporary disease is causing great alarm.

1. very much, exceedingly, Sicikolo wakabasiya bumbi beenzinyina. = The pupil far outstripped his friends. Also: loko, cimbi.
  2. some more, Mukaintu wakaleta
1. busu niyakateta nsima. = The woman brought some more maize-flour when the nsima was not stiff enough.
1. unlawful, Wakatalika kuyanda kujana mali munzila zyabumenemene. = He began to want to find money by unlawful means.
1. many, Bunji bwabo bakali kuboolela buyo kulya nyama. = Many of them had just come to eat meat.

1. How? Muli buti? = How are you? Ino mujika buti nsima? = How do you cook nsima? Also: buyani?
  2. no matter how, Sokwe ulafwambaana kubona cikali nociyubide buti kwiinda banyamanyina boonse. = The mon key is quicker to see danger, no matter how it is concealed, more than all it's fellow animals.
1. that, Butala buya buyanda kuwa. = That granary is about to fall. Tiindazyi kuti buya mbobede pe. = I did not know that that is how you are.
1. How? Ani kukondola bukoko mucita buyani? = Now how do you begin brewing beer. Also: biyani?
1. only, Civwubwe ujanwa
